name: Política de Inteligência Artificial de Defesa (PIAD)
description: The Brazilian Ministry of Defense enacted the Defense Artificial Intelligence Policy (PIAD) via Portaria GM-MD nº 4.360 to promote the development, deployment, and responsible use of AI across the Armed Forces. It aims to build sovereign technological capabilities, reduce dependency on foreign suppliers, and integrate AI into strategic, operational, and tactical military planning, including command and control, cybersecurity, and logistics. Funding is expected to draw from the National Fund for Scientific and Technological Development (FNDCT), which has up to R$ 500 million earmarked for defense technology autonomy projects.
novelty: It is Brazil’s first national policy explicitly framing military AI as systems capable of executing tasks in an “autonomous or assisted” manner within the Armed Forces’ Command and Control Cycle, while mandating technological sovereignty and a convergent, joint approach across the Navy, Army, and Air Force.
stakeholders: The Brazilian Armed Forces (Navy, Army, Air Force), the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation via FNDCT/Finep, and domestic research institutions such as UFMG and the Army Technology Center competing for project funding.
agentic_rationale: The policy defines Defense AI as technologies “capaz de executar, de maneira ‘autônoma ou assistida’, tarefas que convencionalmente exigem inteligência humana” and explicitly inserts AI into the military Command and Control Cycle (Observation, Orientation, Decision, Action) to accelerate decision-making and action against adversaries.
tech_details: The policy covers software, hardware, and systems for pattern recognition, predictive analysis, and process improvement across strategic, operational, and tactical levels. Concrete initiatives mentioned include UFMG’s GeoiDE geoinformation extraction project, the Army’s Integrated AI and Data Platform, and the Navy’s Advanced Operational Research and AI Laboratory, though specific models and infrastructure locations remain undefined.

The framework leverages existing UPI features such as UPI Circle for delegated payment authority and Reserve Pay for blocking funds, initially targeting low-value, frequent purchases with plans for more complex use cases.
novelty: It would create one of the first national infrastructures for agentic transactions globally, distinguishing India from private-sector-led initiatives by payments companies and tech giants.
stakeholders: Consumers, merchants, financial institutions, and the Indian government, with potential to serve as a global blueprint for national agentic payment systems.
agentic_rationale: AI agents would 'assume the heavy lifting for routine transactions' by receiving delegated payment authority through UPI Circle to conduct 'low-value, frequent purchases' independently, with funds blocked via Reserve Pay for multiple debits within set caps.
tech_details: Built atop India's existing UPI real-time payments infrastructure, incorporating the UPI Circle delegated-authority feature and the Reserve Pay fund-blocking capability for controlled agentic debits.

name: Governo Zero Clique
description: Governo Zero Clique is an AI-powered digital system created by Gove and deployed across Brazilian municipalities via WhatsApp and the internet to automate citizen services, reduce bureaucracy, and increase tax revenue. It handles tasks such as appointment scheduling, document issuance, debt negotiation, and answering common questions without requiring in-person visits. Reported results include a 135% increase in overdue tax collection in Areal (RJ), R$20 million in credit recovery in Divinópolis (MG), and 95% of invoice requests resolved automatically in Jacareí (SP).
novelty: The initiative introduces a 'Zero Click' concept where citizens simply send a request via mobile phone and the municipality automatically resolves the entire process end-to-end, eliminating the need for citizens to understand internal bureaucratic procedures or visit public offices. It shifts service delivery from digital attendance to autonomous resolution of complex tasks like debt negotiation and official document issuance.
stakeholders: Citizens of over 100 participating Brazilian municipalities (reaching 16 million people), municipal government staff who are freed from routine tasks, and Gove as the technology provider.
agentic_rationale: The virtual assistant 'resolves problems by itself' (resolve problemas sozinho), autonomously scheduling appointments, issuing tax invoices, negotiating debts, and answering common questions via WhatsApp or the internet without requiring citizens to visit a public building. In Rio Verde (GO) and Jacareí (SP), 95% of service requests and invoice demands are resolved by robots without any human attendant intervention.
tech_details: The system uses artificial intelligence integrated with WhatsApp and web-based channels to deliver automated public services; specific underlying models or technical architecture are not detailed in the source.

name: Uber-Wayve London Robotaxi Launch
description: Uber launched autonomous robotaxi rides in London using Wayve's AI Driver technology, initially deploying fewer than 20 Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles with a licensed safety operator on board. The service matches riders requesting UberX, Uber Comfort or Uber Electric at no additional cost, while a phased rollout is intended to build public and regulatory trust ahead of fully driverless operations that remain pending further authorisation.
novelty: This makes London the second European city after Zagreb to offer Uber robotaxis, and marks the first commercial deployment of Wayve's AI Driver in its home city, ahead of planned entries by Waymo and Baidu. The system uses machine learning to adapt to complex driving environments like a human driver.
stakeholders: London riders using Uber, Uber, Wayve, Transport for London as the authorisation body, and the UK Department for Transport.
agentic_rationale: The Wayve AI Driver autonomously controls the vehicle and independently executes real-time driving maneuvers, learning from experience to adapt to new roads, vehicles, weather conditions and cities without a human initiating each steering or navigation decision. A licensed safety operator sits behind the wheel to monitor operations before future fully driverless approval.
tech_details: Wayve's end-to-end AI Driver is integrated into Ford Mustang Mach-E vehicles and uses machine learning to drive by experience, generalising to new roads, vehicles, weather and cities; it operates via Uber's ride-hailing platform.

novelty: The model achieves frontier-level performance in autonomous vulnerability discovery and automated patching at significantly lower cost than larger frontier models, with specific optimization for defensive cybersecurity operations over offensive capabilities.

tech_details: Powered by long-running agentic loops with recursive evaluation and refinement; trained with rigorous cybersecurity domain focus; available via Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and Fairwind Program for cyber-specific variant.

name: Manatee County AI Procurement Efficiency Pilot
description: An AI pilot program analyzed Manatee County's procurement records covering nearly $2.5 billion in spending and over 147,000 records to identify annual efficiency opportunities estimated between $14.5 million and $49.5 million. Conducted for $4,900 following a state audit, the pilot recommends continuous AI-assisted contract compliance and procurement monitoring.
novelty: The pilot demonstrates autonomous AI agents auditing massive government procurement datasets at very low cost, producing categorized savings estimates with confidence levels. tech_details: The pilot uses DigiBuild's large language model to analyze digital procurement records and vendor contracts. It is designed for continuous monitoring to capture recurring spending patterns in near-real-time, with recommendations for ongoing AI-assisted contract compliance tools.

name: Resilience Intelligence (AEGIS)
organisation: German and European public authorities; Forschungszentrum Jülich
description: Resilience Intelligence is a sovereign Agentic GeoAI platform for crisis management that connects specialized AI agents with geodata from satellites, sensors, drones and situation reports to create a decision-making layer for German and European authorities. It spatially, temporally and semantically fuses multi-source data, orchestrates agentic workflows and embeds human-in-the-loop governance to produce traceable, accountable crisis assessments. The concept originates from the Horizon Europe AEGIS project and is scientifically supported by Forschungszentrum Jülich.
novelty: It proposes a sovereign European intelligence layer that does not merely aggregate data but prepares traceable, human-governed crisis decisions by autonomously fusing heterogeneous satellite, sensor and drone feeds through specialized agents that orchestrate analysis workflows while explicitly surfacing uncertainty and provenance.
stakeholders: Crisis management authorities at federal, state and municipal levels, operators of critical infrastructure, emergency control centres, and the research institutions providing underlying models and HPC infrastructure.
agentic_rationale: Specialized AI agents autonomously translate operational questions into technical analysis paths, select relevant data sources, start appropriate workflows, prioritize information and suggest concrete next steps, so that crisis teams no longer have to monitor ten systems in parallel. As described in the source: 'spezialisierte KI-Agenten operative Fragen in technische Analysewege übersetzen. Relevante Datenquellen werden ausgewählt, passende Workflows gestartet, Informationen priorisiert und konkrete nächste Schritte vorgeschlagen.'
tech_details: Agentic GeoAI platform connecting Copernicus earth observation, Galileo/EGNSS, drone-based verification and local sensor data via specialized AI agents; validated and scaled on European high-performance computing infrastructure (LUMI/EuroHPC) and scientifically supported by Forschungszentrum Jülich, originating from the 36-month Horizon Europe AEGIS project.

It represents a claimed move from traditional bureaucratic process to continuous, 24-hour algorithmic execution of government functions at the highest federal level.

name: Fairwind Program (Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber)
description: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, an AI model for autonomous vulnerability discovery and automated patching, exclusively through the Fairwind Program, which restricts access to vetted government agencies, critical infrastructure operators, and cybersecurity partners via phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and strict access controls. Paired with the CodeMender system in a secure, gated environment, it can autonomously find, verify and fix software vulnerabilities. Early evaluations by the Chrome Security team found it produced correct patches at 2.6 times the rate of comparable commercial models, and Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research team used it to identify a critical foundational vulnerability in under two hours.
novelty: It formalizes access to a dual-use cybersecurity AI behind an institutional accountability framework with explicit eligibility tiers, published operational standards, and a disclosed partner ecosystem—requiring phishing-resistant multifactor authentication and limiting use to internal cybersecurity and incident-response teams rather than standard commercial API access. By packaging the specialized model with the automated CodeMender remediation tool, it signals hyperscalers moving from raw infrastructure to finished, government-ready security capabilities while achieving practical parity with leading frontier models on automated patching at significantly lower cost.
stakeholders: Government agencies, national cyber authorities, critical infrastructure operators in healthcare, telecom, energy and finance, vetted cybersecurity firms including CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Wiz, and incumbent defense contractors such as Palantir that face new competitive pressure.
agentic_rationale: Flash Cyber is purpose-built to autonomously find, verify and fix software vulnerabilities, and is paired with the CodeMender system to deliver automated patching inside a secure environment without a human initiating each step. Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research team leveraged it to identify a critical foundational vulnerability in under two hours—work that typically requires months—and the Chrome Security team found it produced correct patches at 2.6 times the rate of comparable commercial models.
tech_details: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is the second-generation cybersecurity Flash model, offered exclusively through the Google Cloud–based Fairwind Program with strict access controls, usage tracking, and a more permissive safety profile than the general-purpose Flash model to handle advanced offensive-technique knowledge defenders need; it is integrated with Google’s CodeMender system for automated remediation.

name: Australian Social Media Age Verification
description: Implementation of automated biometric age verification to enforce Australia's statutory ban on social media access for users under 16 years old. novelty: Large-scale deployment of outsourced automated biometric identity verification to enforce regulatory age restrictions, where commercial AI systems autonomously determine access eligibility based on sensitive biometric data processing.
stakeholders: Social media platforms operating in Australia, users under 16 and their families, Australian regulatory authorities, and identity verification provider Persona Identities, Inc.
agentic_rationale: The system autonomously extracts facial geometry from government-issued ID documents and real-time selfies, compares biometric features to verify identity and age, and renders automated decisions on access eligibility without human review of individual cases.
tech_details: Facial recognition software that extracts facial features and compares geometric data between ID photos and live selfies; automated document validation for age determination.
